architecture.mechanism: Replacing dichotomous (binary significant/nonsignificant) classification with continuous effect-size-based judgment improves interpretability and value of a system's measurements.
architecture.intervention: Replace the battery pack's binary over-current/thermal-shutoff control logic with a continuous effect-size-based power management algorithm: the BMS grades current delivery proportionally to measured effect sizes (rate of temperature rise, voltage sag magnitude, state-of-charge slope) instead of abruptly cutting or clamping current when a fixed threshold is crossed, so heavy-load discharge is dynamically derated rather than hard-stopped.
architecture.expected_effect: Sustained high-current discharge under heavy load, delivered as graded power instead of abrupt fade/cutoff, extending usable work output through a full shift while keeping cell temperature within safe limits.
architecture.falsification_test: Run two identical cordless drill battery packs (one with binary cutoff firmware, one with effect-size-graded modulation) on a standardized heavy-load duty cycle (e.g., repeated high-torque drilling at constant load until 10% remaining capacity), logging sustained power output, total work done, and peak cell temperature; if the graded pack does not deliver higher average sustained power without exceeding thermal limits, the mechanism is falsified.
